jobs.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. ONE whole original TECHNOMANCIEN player-class sprite for a cyberpunk roguelike, a DARK MACHINE PRIEST who has replaced almost all of his human body with robotics. One complete coherent character from hood crown to soles, genuine transparent background with margins, no shadow, floor, text, logo, weapon, staff, tools, robot pet, extra limbs or props. Almost frontal and balanced with the subtle elevated view of a classic roguelike sprite, no dramatic perspective. Two empty humanoid articulated mechanical hands slightly away from the torso, two distinct mechanical feet. Height about 58 pixels in a 64 by 64 game cell. This is a compact clean game sprite, not a detailed concept illustration. Normal compact head, short neck seated in the shoulders, no long hood, pointed wizard cap, neck stalk, oversized mask or huge head. Anatomically adult slender chassis and a sober vertical coat silhouette. Fully mechanical dark gunmetal face under a close rounded charcoal hood, a simple single amber optic on viewer left and a quiet steel lower face, no visible flesh, no teeth or skull icon. Keep THIS identity throughout the five-stage range.
Visual identity: plain dark ash/charcoal machine-priest vestments, large readable grey folds, a broad muted aubergine-brown INNER cloth panel, smoky steel limbs and quiet pale ash edge planes. Contrast dark cloth against lighter steel and broad ash-grey folds so he is readable on dark ground. Only a few large exposed joints and smooth steel hand/calf masses convey robotics. No bright copper/orange armored chest, no broad square brawler pauldrons, no marine helmet, no muscular human superhero. At heavier stages protect him with a long narrow armored mantle, collar and vertical coat plates instead of the Bastion's broad slab suit.
Very economical matte value planes, two or three tones per material, broad upper-left light, restrained dark outer silhouette, no thick black outlines around every part. Avoid microtexture, rivets, tiny buttons, straps, trim, many pipes, thin hanging cables, ornament, tiny vents, decorative dots, sparks, neon halos and photoreal textures. One small optic is enough. Draw the full body and head together coherently so the cowl touches the shoulders naturally. Preserve negative spaces at arms and between feet even when the coat is heavy. Armor, gloves, lower body and boots all follow the requested protection stage.
STAGE 1 OF 5: very light ritual workwear. Narrow silhouette about 25-27 native pixels wide. A short knee-length split charcoal tabard and soft rounded hood, one broad ash-grey shoulder cloth fold. Exposed narrow gunmetal rib chassis in two or three SIMPLE large mechanical planes, bare mechanical upper arms and lower arms with minimal smooth hand guards, uncovered steel thighs and calves, narrow plain mechanical work boots. No hard shoulder mantle, chest plate, thigh shells or heavy greaves. The cloth is modest and mobile, leaving the mechanical body obvious. Keep the muted aubergine inner tabard visible as one broad calm area. Face remains the same compact fully mechanical single-optic face.
Reference role: this complete middle-tier character is the identity, compact hood, palette, stance and game-sprite rendering reference. Retain the SAME face, single optic and normal head proportions. Redesign the OUTFIT coverage and weight for the specified stage; do not simply duplicate the middle armor. Keep the hood low and close-fitting at all stages, no enlarged pointed crown.
